result.narrative:
Mehtab Agro Foods is showing accumulating payment stress across both of its policies. Two overdue notifications are open: INR 7,700,000 on the supply-chain-finance policy TCI-SCF-2026-0001, logged on 2026-09-20 with the oldest item at 64 days past due, and INR 3,000,000 on the whole-turnover policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, logged on 2026-10-13 at 41 days past due. The payment review marks the trend as deteriorating: notification volume rose from 1 to 2 over the last six months and now spans both policies, against a single prior overdue that resolved in 18 days. No news has been matched to this buyer.

The score of 63.7 is entirely payment-driven: 0.65 x 98.0 (payment, 64 DPD) + 0.35 x 0.0 (news) = 63.7, giving a PD of 0.5892 and a High Risk band. The news component contributes nothing, and as the adjudicator notes, that 0.0 reflects no matched articles and no parent linkage rather than a verified clean record. The payment raw of 98.0 bands High Risk on its own. The adjudicator agreed with the band but attached caveats: the payment review states INR 6.0M of combined overdue while the underlying notifications record INR 7,700,000 and INR 3,000,000 separately; it gives the oldest item an original due date of 2026-09-20, the same date it was already logged at 64 days past due; and the scored 64 DPD predates the 2026-10-13 notification, so the aging input may be stale. All three discrepancies point toward equal or greater risk, so the band stands, but exposure and aging should be re-sourced from the notifications.

Both lines are recommended for reduction to the point where expected loss meets the 25% appetite, against a PD of 0.5892. On TCI-SCF-2026-0001 (insured: Meridia Bank) the limit falls from INR 15,000,000 to INR 7,700,000, taking expected loss from 6,363,360 down to 3,266,525. On TCI-WT-2026-0002 (insured: Orvana Steel) the limit falls from INR 8,000,000 to INR 3,394,433, taking expected loss from 3,393,792 down to 1,440,000. Maximum liability does not bind on either line. Given the adjudicator's exposure caveat, confirm the true overdue balances before the reductions are issued, since the SCF revised limit is set at the owed figure.

This is the top band, so improvement has to come from the payment side alone: the score needs to fall 13.7 points to drop below 50.0 into Watch, and with news contributing 0.0 there is no other lever. Clearing or substantially aging down the 64-day item on TCI-SCF-2026-0001 and settling the 41-day item on TCI-WT-2026-0002 would do it, as would a return to the 18-day resolution pattern seen in the single prior case. A clean re-sourcing of the notifications showing a lower overdue balance and no further accumulation would also support revisiting the limits.
